# Root accepted scoped join: calibrated terminal-noise thermal loading

1 November2026. Qualified internal mathematical acceptance; no experimental or independent peer-review claim.

## Precisely earned operation
For the actual recursive commuting code at a sufficiently low fixed temperature, take a SUPPLIED encoded input and a specified final layer of independent calibrated bounded-support Pauli faults. If fault probabilities are sufficiently small relative to temperature and local energy changes, a positive, polynomially sampleable pre-distorted syndrome distribution produces the ideal thermal logical encoding AFTER that final noise layer, up to a stretched-exponentially small logical-frame error and separately charged sampling/calibration errors.

Let M=O(n) be the number of fault labels and b_n=poly(n)exp(-c n^eta) the uniform enlarged bad-syndrome bound. If sampler TV error is epsilon, calibration rates qhat_i differ from actual q_i, and a separate input/preparation discrepancy is delta_in, the output reference-safe trace-norm discrepancy is bounded by
 delta_in + 2epsilon + 2M b_n + 2 sum_i |q_i-qhat_i|.
The input discrepancy must be genuinely supplied/earned; generic noisy FT encoding is NOT presumed to reduce to independent Pauli noise. A calibration-confidence failure adds its charged bad-event contribution. Subsequent common storage/decoding channels add this loading discrepancy once by contractivity, not multiplied by storage duration.

The applicable passive hold theorem here is the independently admitted COMMUTING thermal model. This does not initialize the actual noncommuting Gibbs state used by the earlier exact-spin-environment result.

## Mechanism
For the syndrome-noise channel C=product_i[(1-q_i)I+q_i F_i], prepare pi_pre=C^(-1)pi_G. The inverse is algebraically signed, but a uniform signed error-island expansion proves pi_pre and ALL partial-inverse distributions positive at sufficiently small fixed noise.

At each partial-noise stage, the syndrome marginal equals the inverse of the remaining noise factors applied to pi_G. Uniform local potential bounds preserve the source's Peierls witness estimate for every prefix. Correctability on the good syndrome set controls the logical frame through all prefixes; matching final syndrome statistics alone would not suffice.

The actual decoder-trace representation makes pi_pre a POSITIVE hard-core p

# Reviewed wording clarification

The whole-join auditor requested replacing the phrase “Each partial-noise history” by the averaged-stage statement. The current join now says “At each partial-noise stage, the syndrome marginal equals the inverse of the remaining noise factors applied to pi_G.” The prefix identity is for the ensemble marginal, not an individual trajectory. No bounds or assumptions change.
